answer: ICE candidates reveal the NAT type and network path, classifying the device's network position. A farm behind one NAT shares one classification, so 141 aliases need 141 distinct network positions. Candidates are gathered fresh each epoch, and the classification is compared to the enrolled one. The plume check runs in the open: 141 fakes pay the full price 141 times, one honest agent pays once, and the nadir trail in the ledger makes the walnut cost visible to everyone.
